summary: S. M. Natesa Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. Around 1883, he worked at the Archaeological Survey of India as assistant to Robert Sewell, and he taught Chembai Vaidyanatha Bhagavatar.

Working in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, S. N. Balagangadhara studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch. He served as a director at Ghent University (~1991–2017) and co-chair at the American Academy of Religion (2004–2007).
S. N. Krishna is an Indologist who studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva, attested in 2026.
S. N. Savadi was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.
Shrinivas Narayan Tadpatrikar was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1939 and serving as Supervisor of Collations in 1942.

Working in Indology, history, and archaeology, S. Rajavelu served as Assistant Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2011) and as Professor in the Department of Marine Archaeology at Tamil University (attested 2015).
Indologist S. S. Janaki studied under Thomas Burrow around 1968–1971. From circa 1974 to 1999, she served as a supervisor and guide at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri worked in philosophy and Indology at the University of Madras, where he was attested as Reader in Indian Philosophy in 1929 and as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy in 1942.

S. Sankaranarayanan worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1986–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

S. Sankararama Sastri was an Indologist who served as a Pandit in the Publication Section of the Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1943) and as a Pandit at the University of Kerala (attested 1944).

S. Sepideh Hosseini works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned a bachelor's degree at Islamic Azad University, Damavand Branch, and completed an Indian language course at the University of Tehran.

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, S. Srikanta Sastri studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1923–1926) under M. H. Krishna. He held a post at the University of Mysore (~1926–1960) and taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.
S. Swaminathan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under J. Sundaram and served as Deputy Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India until retiring by 2013.

Working in religious studies and socio-cultural anthropology, Saba Mahmood studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University (PhD ~1992–1998). She held posts at the University of Chicago (~1999–2004) and UC Berkeley (2004–2018), and taught Thomas Borchert.

Sabine Löhr, working in Indology and philosophy, studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg (M.A.), completing doctoral studies under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a research assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft) at the University of Hamburg.
Sabriye Tenberken, a Tibetology scholar, studied at the University of Bonn (~1990–1997) and founded Braille Without Borders.

Saburō Hasegawa studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929). He taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (~1954–1957) and California College of the Arts (~1955–1957), and counted Alan Watts among his students.
Sachin Kathale works in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. He earned an M.Phil. from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and has served as a teacher at Samskrita Bharati.

Working in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Sadajiro Sugiura studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D.), and Episcopal Divinity School. He held posts at Penn, the Army War College (1903), and Rikkyo University, including lecturer and professor emeritus.

Sadananda Das works in Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from Central Sanskrit University (Shastri, 1989) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (M.A. 1991, Ph.D. 2002), and became a lecturer at the University of Leipzig in 2005.
